I have farmed 30 years, so I will not start from empty talk. I will start from what has held yield for me before and what I see around me. With 20 mu and well water, I will keep the land in cabbage through the year, because cabbage brings cash faster than wheat and maize on my ground. Wheat and maize are steadier, but they tie up land longer, and if I switch away from cabbage I lose money from the better crop. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than let the heads stay small. For cabbage I will feed the land heavy, water on time, and spray when worms and rot start showing. I will plough before the first crop, then use rotary tillage between the next cabbage crops to save labor. Since there are only 2 people in my house, I will keep the work simple and stick to one main line of cropping instead of spreading myself thin. This year I will not put area into maize or wheat, even though I have grown them before, because my cabbage-cabbage-cabbage way fits my land, my water, and my money better.
